youtube.title: Why the Silent Player Took Everything #Shorts
youtube.description:
June hasn't said a word all night. She's about to take everything.

In a negotiation study, silent pauses of three seconds or more went with more value created for both sides, and people told to use silence created more value too. The pause didn't work by intimidation: it seemed to work as thinking time, with less 'fixed pie' thinking (Curhan et al., 2022, Journal of Applied Psychology). But silence is hard: even a four-second gap in a conversation can make people feel uneasy (Koudenburg et al., 2011).

Could you stay quiet for three whole seconds?

Sources:
- Curhan, Overbeck, Cho, Zhang & Yang (2022), Silence is golden: Extended silence, deliberative mindset, and value creation in negotiation, J. Applied Psychology 107(1): https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/144112
- MIT Sloan, In negotiation, use silence to improve outcomes for all: https://mitsloan.mit.edu/ideas-made-to-matter/negotiation-use-silence-to-improve-outcomes-all
- Koudenburg, Postmes & Gordijn (2011), Disrupting the flow, J. Exp. Social Psychology: https://www.rug.nl/news/2011/01/009_stiltes?lang=en

June, Max and the game night are fictional.
AI disclosure: made with AI assistance (script drafting, synthetic narration voice, animation).
